paragraphs.sourceText: The robotics revolution is set to bring humans face to face with an old fear—man-made creations as smart and capable as we are but without a moral compass. As robots take on ever more complex roles, the question naturally 26 : Who will be responsible when they do something wrong? Manufacturers? Users? Software writers? The answer depends on the robot.

Robots already save us time, money and energy. In the future, they will improve our health care, social welfare and standard of living. The 27 of computational power and engineering advances will 28 enable lower-cost in- home care for the disabled, 29 use of driverless cars that may reduce drunk- and distracted-driving accidents and countless home and service-industry uses for robots, from street cleaning to food preparation.

But there are 30 to be problems. Robot cars will crash. A drone ( 遥控飞行器 ) operator will 31 someone’s privacy. A robotic lawn mower will run over a neighbor’s cat. Juries sympathetic to the 32 of machines will punish entrepreneurs with company-crushing 33 and damages. What should governments do to protect people while 34 space for innovation?

Big, complicated systems on which much public safety depends, like driverless cars, should be built, 35 and sold by manufacturers who take responsibility for ensuring safety and are liable for accidents. Governments should set safety requirements and then let insurers price the risk of the robots based on the manufacturer’s driving record, not the passenger’s.

Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Reform and Medical Costs
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。在答题卡上标记相应字母来回答问题 2. 改革和医疗费用

paragraphs.sourceText: A. Americans are deeply concerned about the relentless rise in health care costs and health insurance premiums. They need to know if reform will help solve the problem. The answer is that no one has an easy fix for rising medical costs. The fundamental fix—reshaping how care is delivered and how doctors are paid in a wasteful, abnormal system—is likely to be achieved only through trial and error and incremental ( 渐进的 ) gains.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：美国人对医疗保健费用和健康保险费的不断上涨深感担忧。他们需要知道改革是否有助于解决问题。答案是，没有人能够轻松解决不断上涨的医疗费用。根本性的解决办法——在一个浪费的、不正常的系统中重塑医疗服务的提供方式以及医生的报酬方式——可能只能通过反复试验和渐进的收益来实现。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. The good news is that a bill just approved by the House and a bill approved by the Senate Finance Committee would implement or test many reforms that should help slow the rise in medical costs over the long term. As a report in The New England Journal of Medicine concluded, “Pretty much every proposed innovation found in the health policy Iiterature these days is contained in these measures.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 好消息是，众议院刚刚批准的一项法案和参议院财政委员会批准的一项法案将实施或测试许多改革，从长远来看，这些改革将有助于减缓医疗费用的上涨。正如《新英格兰医学杂志》的一篇报告所总结的那样，“当今卫生政策文献中发现的几乎所有拟议的创新都包含在这些措施中。”

paragraphs.sourceText: C. Medical spending, which typically rises faster than wages and the overall economy, is propelled by two things: the high prices charged for medical services in this country and the volume of unnecessary care delivered by doctors and hospitals, which often perform a lot more tests and treatments than a patient really needs.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 医疗支出的增长速度通常快于工资和整体经济的增长，它是由两件事推动的：这个国家的医疗服务收费高，以及医生和医院提供的不必要的护理量，这些检查和治疗往往比患者真正需要的要多得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Here are some of the important proposals in the House and Senate bills to try to address those problems, and why it is hard to know how well they will work.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 以下是众议院和参议院法案中试图解决这些问题的一些重要提案，以及为什么很难知道它们的效果如何。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Both bills would reduce the rate of growth in annual Medicare payments to hospitals, nursing homes and other providers by amounts comparable to the productivity savings routinely made in other industries with the help of new technologies and new ways to organize work. This proposal could save Medicare more than $100 billion over the next decade. If private plans demanded similar productivity savings from providers, and refused to let providers shift additional costs to them, the savings could be much larger. Critics say Congress will give in to lobbyists and let inefficient providers off the hook (放过). That is far less likely to happen if Congress also adopts strong “pay-go” rules requiring that any increase in payments to providers be offset by new taxes or budget cuts.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 这两项法案都将降低向医院、疗养院和其他提供者提供的年度医疗保险付款的增长率，其金额与其他行业在新技术和新的工作组织方式的帮助下通常节省的生产力相当。该提案可以在未来十年为医疗保险节省超过 1000 亿美元。如果私人计划要求提供商提供类似的生产力节省，并且拒绝让提供商将额外成本转嫁给他们，那么节省的费用可能会大得多。批评者称，国会将向游说者让步，让效率低下的供应商摆脱困境。如果国会还采用强有力的“现收现付”规则，要求向提供商支付的任何增加费用都必须通过新的税收或预算削减来抵消，那么这种情况发生的可能性就小得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. The Senate Finance bill would impose an excise tax ( 消费税 ) on health insurance plans that cost more than $8,000 for an individual or $21,000 for a family. It would most likely cause insurers to redesign plans to fall beneath the threshold. Enrollees would have to pay more money for many services out of their own pockets, and that would encourage them to think twice about whether an expensive or redundant test was worth it. Economists project that most employers would shift money from expensive health benefits into wages, The House bill has no similar tax. The final legislation should.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 参议院财政法案将对个人费用超过 8,000 美元或家庭费用超过 21,000 美元的健康保险计划征收消费税 (消费税)。这很可能会导致保险公司重新设计计划以低于门槛。注册者将不得不自掏腰包为许多服务支付更多费用，这将鼓励他们三思而行，昂贵或多余的测试是否值得。经济学家预计，大多数雇主会将资金从昂贵的医疗福利转向工资，但众议院法案没有类似的税收。最终立法应该。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. Any doctor who has wrestled with multiple forms from different insurers, or patients who have tried to understand their own parade of statements, know that simplification ought to save money. When the health insurance industry was still cooperating in reform efforts, its trade group offered to provide standardized forms for automated processing. It estimated that step would save hundreds of billions of dollars over the next decade. The bills would lock that pledge into law.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 任何曾与不同保险公司的多种表格进行过斗争的医生，或试图理解自己的一系列陈述的患者都知道，简化应该可以省钱。当健康保险行业仍在配合改革时，其行业集团提出提供自动化处理的标准化表格。据估计，这一举措将在未来十年节省数千亿美元。这些法案将把这一承诺写入法律。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. The stimulus package provided money to convert the inefficient, paper-driven medical system to electronic records that can be easily viewed and transmitted. This requires open investments to help doctors convert. In time it should help restrain costs by eliminating redundant tests, preventing drug interactions, and helping doctors find the best treatments.
paragraphs.translationZh: H.刺激计划提供资金，将低效、纸质驱动的医疗系统转换为易于查看和传输的电子记录。这需要开放投资来帮助医生转变。随着时间的推移，它应该通过消除多余的测试、防止药物相互作用并帮助医生找到最佳治疗方法来帮助控制成本。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Virtually all experts agree that the fee-for-service system—doctors are rewarded for the quantity of care rather than its quality or effectiveness—is a primary reason that the cost of care is so high. Most agree that the solution is to push doctors to accept fixed payments to care for a particular illness or for a patient’s needs over a year. No one knows how to make that happen quickly. The bills in both houses would start pilot projects within Medicare. They include such measures as accountable care organizations to take charge of a patient’s needs with an eye on both cost and quality, and chronic disease management to make sure the seriously ill, who are responsible for the bulk of all health care costs, are treated properly. For the most part, these experiments rely on incentive payments to get doctors to try them.
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 几乎所有专家都认为，按服务收费制度（医生根据护理数量而不是质量或有效性获得奖励）是护理成本如此之高的主要原因。大多数人认为，解决方案是推动医生接受固定付款来治疗特定疾病或满足患者一年以上的需求。没有人知道如何快速实现这一目标。两院的法案将启动医疗保险范围内的试点项目。其中包括诸如负责任的护理组织等措施，负责照顾患者的需求，同时关注成本和质量；以及慢性病管理，以确保承担所有医疗保健费用大部分的重病患者得到适当的治疗。在很大程度上，这些实验依靠奖励金来吸引医生进行尝试。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. Testing innovations do no good unless the good experiments are identified and expanded and the bad ones are dropped. The Senate bill would create an independent commission to monitor the pilot programs and recommend changes in Medicare’s payment policies to urge providers to adopt reforms that work. The changes would have to be approved or rejected as a whole by Congress, making it hard for narrow-interest lobbies to bend lawmakers to their will.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 测试创新没有任何好处，除非好的实验能够被识别和扩大，坏的实验被放弃。参议院法案将设立一个独立委员会来监督试点计划，并建议改变医疗保险的支付政策，以敦促提供者采取有效的改革。这些改变必须得到国会的整体批准或拒绝，这使得狭隘利益游说团体很难让立法者屈服于他们的意愿。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. The bills in both chambers would create health insurance exchanges on which small businesses and individuals could choose from an array of private plans and possibly a public option. All the plans would have to provide standard benefit packages that would be easy to compare. To get access to millions of new customers, insurers would have a strong incentive to sell on the exchange. And the head-to-head competition might give them a strong incentive to lower their prices, perhaps by accepting slimmer profit margins or demanding better deals from providers.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 参众两院的法案将创建健康保险交易所，小企业和个人可以在其中从一系列私人计划和可能的公共选项中进行选择。所有计划都必须提供易于比较的标准福利方案。为了获得数百万新客户，保险公司将有强烈的动机在交易所进行销售。面对面的竞争可能会给他们带来降低价格的强烈动机，也许是通过接受更薄的利润率或要求供应商提供更好的交易。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. The final legislation might throw a public plan into the competition, but thanks to the fierce opposition of the insurance industry and Republican critics, it might not save much money. The one in the House bill would have to negotiate rates with providers, rather than using Medicare rates, as many reformers wanted.
paragraphs.translationZh: L.最终的立法可能会将一项公共计划投入竞争，但由于保险业和共和党批评者的强烈反对，它可能不会节省多少钱。众议院法案中的一项必须与医疗服务提供者协商费率，而不是像许多改革者希望的那样使用医疗保险费率。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. The president’s stimulus package is pumping money into research to compare how well various treatments work. Is surgery, radiation or careful monitoring best for prostate ( 前列腺) cancer? Is the latest and most expensive cholesterol-lowering drug any better than its common competitors? The pending bills would spend additional money to accelerate this effort.
paragraphs.translationZh: M. 总统的经济刺激计划正在向研究注入资金，以比较各种治疗方法的效果。手术、放疗或仔细监测是治疗前列腺癌的最佳方法吗？最新、最昂贵的降胆固醇药物是否比其常见竞争对手更好？悬而未决的法案将花费额外的资金来加速这一努力。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. Critics have charged that this sensible idea would lead to rationing of care. (That would be true only if you believed that patients should have an unrestrained right to treatments proven to be inferior.) As a result, the bills do not require, as they should, that the results of these studies be used to set payment rates in Medicare.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 批评者指责这一明智的想法会导致护理配给。 （只有当你相信患者应该拥有不受限制的权利来接受被证明较差的治疗时，这才是正确的。）因此，这些法案并不要求（正如它们应该的那样）将这些研究的结果用于设定医疗保险的支付率。

paragraphs.sourceText: O. Congress needs to find the courage to allow Medicare to pay preferentially for treatments proven to be superior. Sometimes the best treatment might be the most expensive. But overall, we suspect that spending would come down through elimination of a lot of unnecessary or even dangerous tests and treatments. [P] The House bill would authorize the secretary of health and human services to negotiate drug prices in Medicare and Medicaid. Some authoritative analysts doubt that the secretary would get better deals than private insurers already get. We believe negotiation could work. It does in other countries. [Q] Missing from these bills is any serious attempt to rein in malpractice costs. Malpractice awards do drive up insurance premiums for doctors in high-risk specialties, and there is some evidence that doctors engage in “defensive medicine” by performing tests and treatments primarily to prove they are not negligent should they get sued.
paragraphs.translationZh: O. 国会需要鼓起勇气，允许医疗保险优先支付被证明是优越的治疗方法。有时最好的治疗可能是最昂贵的。但总的来说，我们怀疑通过消除大量不必要的甚至危险的测试和治疗，支出将会下降。 [P] 众议院法案将授权卫生与公众服务部部长就医疗保险和医疗补助中的药品价格进行谈判。一些权威分析人士怀疑，这位部长能否获得比私人保险公司已经获得的更好的交易。我们相信谈判能够奏效。在其他国家也是如此。 [问] 这些法案中缺少任何旨在控制医疗事故成本的认真尝试。医疗事故赔偿确实会推高高风险专业医生的保险费，而且有一些证据表明，医生通过进行检查和治疗来从事“防御性医学”，主要是为了证明他们在被起诉时没有疏忽。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. With a tax imposed on expensive health insurance plans, most employers will likely transfer money from health expenses into wages.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 由于对昂贵的健康保险计划征税，大多数雇主可能会将钱从医疗费用转入工资。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Changes in policy would be approved or rejected as a whole so that lobbyists would find it hard to influence lawmakers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 政策的改变将被整体批准或拒绝，这样游说者就会发现很难影响立法者。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. It is not easy to curb the rising medical costs in America.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 遏制美国不断上涨的医疗费用并不容易。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Standardization of forms for automatic processing will save a lot of medical expenses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 自动处理表格标准化将节省大量医疗费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Republicans and the insurance industry are strongly opposed to the creation of a public insurance plan.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 共和党人和保险业强烈反对制定公共保险计划。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Conversion of paper to electronic medical records will help eliminate redundant tests and prevent drug interactions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 将纸质病历转换为电子病历将有助于消除多余的测试并防止药物相互作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. The high cost of medical services and unnecessary tests and treatments have driven up medical expenses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 高昂的医疗服务费用以及不必要的检查和治疗推高了医疗费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. One main factor that has driven up medical expenses is that doctors are compensated for the amount of care rather than its effect.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 推高医疗费用的一个主要因素是医生根据护理量而不是效果获得补偿。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Contrary to analysts’ doubts, the author believes drug prices may be lowered through negotiation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 与分析师的疑虑相反，作者认为药品价格可能会通过谈判降低。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Fair competition might create a strong incentive for insurers to charge less.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 公平竞争可能会强烈激励保险公司降低收费。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are two passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the center.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有两个段落。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选项，并在答题纸 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Facing water shortages and escalating fertilizer costs, farmers in developing countries are using raw sewage ( 下水道污水 ) to irrigate and fertilize nearly 49 million acres of cropland, according to a new report—and it may not be a bad thing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一份新的报告显示，面对水资源短缺和不断上涨的化肥成本，发展中国家的农民正在使用原污水（下水道污水）来灌溉和施肥近 4900 万英亩的农田，这可能不是一件坏事。

paragraphs.sourceText: While the practice carries serious health risks for many, those dangers are outweighed by the social and economic gains for poor urban farmers and consumers who need affordable food. “There is a large potential for wastewater agriculture to both help and hurt great numbers of urban consumers,” said Liqa Raschid-Sally, who led the study.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然这种做法给许多人带来了严重的健康风险，但贫困城市农民和需要负担得起的食物的消费者所获得的社会和经济收益超过了这些危险。该研究的领导者 Liqa Raschid-Sally 表示：“废水农业在帮助和伤害大量城市消费者方面有着巨大的潜力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The report focused on poor urban areas, where farms in or near cities supply relatively inexpensive food. Most of these operations draw irrigation water from local rivers or lakes. Unlike developed cities, however, these areas lack advanced water-treatment facilities, and rivers effectively become sewers ( 下水道 ).
paragraphs.translationZh: 该报告重点关注贫困城市地区，城市内或城市附近的农场提供相对便宜的食品。大多数这些作业从当地河流或湖泊抽取灌溉水。然而，与发达城市不同的是，这些地区缺乏先进的水处理设施，河流实际上变成了下水道。

paragraphs.sourceText: When this water is used for agricultural irrigation, farmers risk absorbing disease-causing becteria, as do consumers who eat the produce raw and unwashed. Nearly 2.2 million people die a year because of diarrhea-related ( 与腹泻相关的) diseases, according to WHO statistics. More than 80% of those cases can be attributed to contact with contaminated water and a lack of proper sanitation. But Pay Drechsel, an environmental scientist, argues that the social and economic benefits of using untreated human waste to grow food outweigh the health risks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当这些水用于农业灌溉时，农民面临着吸收致病细菌的风险，生吃未经清洗的农产品的消费者也是如此。据世界卫生组织统计，每年有近 220 万人死于腹泻相关疾病。其中 80% 以上的病例可归因于接触受污染的水和缺乏适当的卫生设施。但环境科学家佩·德雷克塞尔 (Pay Drechsel) 认为，利用未经处理的人类排泄物种植粮食的社会和经济效益超过了健康风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: Those dangers can be addressed with farmer and consumer education, he said, while the free water and nutrients from human waste can help urban farmers in developing countries to escape poverty.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他说，这些危险可以通过农民和消费者教育来解决，而人类排泄物中的免费水和营养物质可以帮助发展中国家的城市农民摆脱贫困。

paragraphs.sourceText: Agriculture is a water-intensive business, accounting for nearly 70% of global fresh water consumption.
paragraphs.translationZh: 农业是耗水行业，占全球淡水消耗量的近70%。

paragraphs.sourceText: In poor, dry regions, untreated wastewater is the only viable irrigation source to keep farmers in business. In some cases, water is so scarce that farmers break open sewage pipes transporting waste to local rivers. Irrigation is the primary agricultural use of human waste in the developing world. But frequently untreated human waste harvested from lavatories is delivered to farms and spread as fertilizer.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在贫穷、干旱的地区，未经处理的废水是维持农民生意的唯一可行的灌溉来源。在某些情况下，水资源非常稀缺，以至于农民打开污水管道将废物运送到当地河流。灌溉是发展中国家人类排泄物的主要农业用途。但从厕所收集的未经处理的人类排泄物常常被运往农场并作为肥料传播。

paragraphs.sourceText: In most cases, the human waste is used on grain crops, which are eventually cooked, minimizing the risk of transmitting water-borne diseases. With fertilizer prices jumping nearly 50% per metric ton over the last year in some places, human waste is an attractive, and often necessary, alternative.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在大多数情况下，人类排泄物被用于谷物作物，最终被煮熟，从而最大限度地减少传播水传播疾病的风险。去年，在某些地方，化肥价格每吨上涨近 50%，人类排泄物成为一种有吸引力且往往是必要的替代品。

paragraphs.sourceText: In cases where sewage mud is used, expensive chemical fertilizer use can be avoided. The mud contains the same critical nutrients.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在使用污水污泥的情况下，可以避免使用昂贵的化肥。泥浆含有相同的关键营养物质。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Overly strict standards often fail,” James Bartram, a WHO water-health expert, said. “We need to accept that fact across much of the planet, so waste with little or no treatment will be used in agriculture for good reason.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “过于严格的标准往往会失败，”世界卫生组织水健康专家詹姆斯·巴特拉姆(James Bartram)说。 “我们需要在地球上的大部分地区接受这一事实，因此未经处理或未经处理的废物将有充分理由用于农业。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: These days, nobody needs to cook. Families graze on high-cholesterol take-aways and microwaved ready-meals. Cooking is an occasional hobby and a vehicle for celebrity chefs. Which makes it odd that the kitchen has become the heart of the modern house: what the great hall was to the medieval castle, the kitchen is to the 21st-century home. The money spent on kitchens has risen with their status. In America the kitchen market is now worth $170 billion, 5 times the country’s film industry. In the year to August 2007, IKEA, a Swedish furniture chain, sold over one million kitchens worldwide. The average budget for a “major” kitchen overhaul in 2006, calculates Remodeling magazine, was a staggering $54,000; even a “minor” improvement cost on average $18,000.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如今，没有人需要做饭。家庭成员吃的是高胆固醇外卖和微波炉加热的即食食品。烹饪是名厨的一种偶尔的爱好和手段。奇怪的是，厨房已成为现代住宅的核心：就像大厅之于中世纪城堡一样，厨房之于 21 世纪的住宅。随着厨房地位的提高，花在厨房上的钱也随之增加。在美国，厨房市场目前价值 1700 亿美元，是该国电影业的 5 倍。截至 2007 年 8 月的一年里，瑞典家具连锁店宜家在全球销售了超过 100 万套厨房。据 Remodeling 杂志计算，2006 年“重大”厨房大修的平均预算高达 54,000 美元，令人震惊；即使是“微小”的改进，平均也要花费 18,000 美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: Exclusivity, more familiar in the world of high fashion, has reached the kitchen: Robinson & Cornish, a British manufacturer of custom-made kitchens, offers a Georgian-style one which would cost £145,000–155,000— excluding building, plumbing and electrical work. Its big selling point is that nobody else will have it: “You won’t see this kitchen anywhere else in the world.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 在高级时尚界更为人熟知的排他性已经延伸到了厨房：英国定制厨房制造商 Robinson & Cornish 提供了一款乔治亚风格的厨房，售价为 145,000 至 155,000 英镑——不包括建筑、管道和电气工程。它的一大卖点是其他人不会拥有它：“你在世界其他任何地方都不会看到这个厨房。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The elevation of the room that once belonged only to the servants to that of design showcase for the modern family tells the story of a century of social change. Right into the early 20th century, kitchens were smoky, noisy places, generally located underground, or to the back of the house, and as far from living space as possible. That was as it should be: kitchens were for servants, and the aspiring middle classes wanted nothing to do with them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 曾经只属于仆人的房间，如今被提升为现代家庭的设计展示柜，讲述着一个世纪社会变迁的故事。到了 20 世纪初期，厨房都是烟雾缭绕、嘈杂的地方，通常位于地下或房子的后面，并尽可能远离居住空间。本来应该如此：厨房是为仆人准备的，有抱负的中产阶级不想与它们有任何关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: But as the working classes prospered and the servant shortage set in, housekeeping became a matter of interest to the educated classes. One of the pioneers of a radical new way of thinking about the kitchen was Catharine Esther Beecher, sister of Harriet Beecher Stowe. In American Woman’s Home, published in 1869, the Beecher sisters recommended a scientific approach to household management, designed to enhance the efficiency of a woman’s work and promote order.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但随着工人阶级的繁荣和仆人短缺的出现，家政服务成为受过教育的阶级的兴趣所在。凯瑟琳·埃丝特·比彻 (Catharine Esther Beecher) 是哈丽特·比彻·斯托 (Harriet Beecher Stowe) 的妹妹，她是厨房全新​​思考方式的先驱之一。在 1869 年出版的《美国妇女之家》中，比彻姐妹推荐了一种科学的家庭管理方法，旨在提高妇女的工作效率并促进秩序。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many contemporary ideas about kitchen design can be traced back to another American, Christine Frederick, who set about enhancing the efficiency of the housewife. Her 1919 work, Household Engineering: Scientific Management in the Home, was based on detailed observation of a housewife’s daily routine. She borrowed the principle of efficiency on the factory floor and applied it to domestic tasks on the kitchen floor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 关于厨房设计的许多当代想法可以追溯到另一位美国人克里斯蒂娜·弗雷德里克（Christine Frederick），她致力于提高家庭主妇的效率。她 1919 年的作品《家庭工程：家庭科学管理》基于对家庭主妇日常生活的详细观察。她借鉴了工厂车间的效率原则，并将其应用到厨房的家务劳动中。

paragraphs.sourceText: Frederick’s central idea, that “stove, sink and kitchen table must be placed in such a relation that useless steps are avoided entirely,” inspired the first fully fitted kitchen, designed in the 1920s by Margarete Schütter-Lihotsky. It was a modernist triumph, and many elements remain central features of today’s kitchen.
paragraphs.translationZh: Frederick 的中心思想是“炉灶、水槽和厨房桌子必须以这样的关系放置，完全避免无用的步骤”，这启发了 Margarete Schütter-Lihotsky 在 1920 年代设计的第一个设备齐全的厨房。这是现代主义的胜利，许多元素仍然是当今厨房的核心特征。
